messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] realtime-p99-detector triggered for prod: p99 latency > 1.5s for 2m across streaming endpoints (route: /v1/stream). Alert id: a9f3. Auto-page -> oncall-amber :rotating_light:
oncall-amber: Ack. I'm on it. Joining the bridge in 1m. Anyone seeing related deploys?
sre-luca: Noted. Pulling graphs: prod-latency/grafana/dashboard#streaming-p95p99 (link) — p95 up from 220ms -> 420ms, p99 jumped to ~1.7s. Tail shows spikes on long seq jobs (seq_len > 1024).
eng-runtime-maya: We pushed a batching tuning to canary 10% ~25m ago (dynamic-batching v2). Could be related. Rolling back canary would be quick if needed.
ml-ops-ryan: Also rolled a re-quantized variant (q8) for one model shard earlier; but that was behind feature flag and only on canary. Checking model routing logs...
prod-sr-samantha: Received first customer report ~2m ago: streaming sessions stutter, some partial chunks delayed. No errors reported, just delayed responses.
cs-jorge: Notified one enterprise customer in EMEA who reported impact to live chat agents. They're seeing ~3-4s delays for long messages. Asking for ETA.
oncall-amber: Quick checks: CPU/GPU utilization look normal, no single host OOMs. Network p95 stable. KV cache hitrate dropped ~30% coincident with spike. That could explain extra compute.
sre-luca: Good catch. KV cache evictions timeline lines up with canary rollout timestamp. Fetching the logs for cache misses.
eng-runtime-maya: If cache invalidation happened from model switch, requests might be cold. We can temporary force prefix caching to on for affected routes or rollback canary. I prefer rollback to isolate.
ml-ops-ryan: Confirmed: route /v1/stream had routing to model-id: redwood-open-3-q8-canary. Cache keys differ for that variant. Hitrate dropped from 88% -> 54% after canary.
oncall-amber: Plan: 1) rollback dynamic-batching canary (quick) 2) if not resolved, rollback model canary 3) open targeted fallback to dedicated pool in parallel if latency persists. Thoughts? :thumbsup:
sre-luca: +1 on rollback dynamic-batching first. That'll revert batching to conservative config (max_batch 16 -> 8) and should reduce scheduling tail risk.
eng-runtime-maya: I'll trigger the rollback now. deploy-bot: rollback triggered for service: runtime-batching-config, from deployment id: dpl-782 to dpl-779 by @eng-runtime-maya.
eng-runtime-maya: Rolling back...
(about 90s pass)
eng-runtime-maya: rollback complete. Observability: p95 trending down to 260ms, p99 down to ~900ms — improving but still above baseline.
sre-luca: KV cache hitrate recovering slowly back to ~72%. Looks like the model canary still causes some cold paths due to q8 key differences. Might need to pin routing.
ml-ops-ryan: We can temporarily pin traffic for /v1/stream to the stable model variant (redwood-open-3-v1) until we reconcile keys. Patching routing table now.
oncall-amber: Patch applied. traffic shift 100% -> stable model.
eng-runtime-maya: Observability after shift: p95 240ms, p99 430ms. Streaming stalls mostly gone. Nice.
prod-sr-samantha: CS: Customer update prepared — "We identified a canary change impacting streaming caching and rolled back. Service restored."
cs-jorge: Sending to affected customers now, offering incident follow-up and timeline.
eng-runtime-maya: Root cause hypothesis: canary introduced model variant with different cache key serialization -> mass cache misses -> extra KV lookups + bigger compute paths exposing scheduling tail. Action items: 1) Add canary gating for cache-key compatibility tests 2) prevent model-routing during dynamic-batching experiments 3) add alert for sudden KV cache hitrate drop correlated with p99 spikes.
sre-luca: Also add a synthetic long-seq streaming test to the regression suite and an automated quick-rollback playbook.
oncall-amber: I'll open a postmortem ticket and assign owners. Short blameless summary to follow. For oncall: changing status -> resolved. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident a9f3 marked RESOLVED by oncall-amber. Duration: ~8m. Pager duty incident closed.
eng-runtime-maya: Small follow-up: we should run through an attribution check to ensure no customer data was re-computed or logged incorrectly during cold misses.
ml-ops-ryan: I'll take that and verify model routing logs / cache population artifacts.
prod-sr-samantha: I'll draft customer-facing post and coordinate with legal if needed.
cs-jorge: Customers notified. None escalated to outage so far.
oncall-amber: final note — nice quick rollback and cross-team comms. Leaving channel.
(ends)
